Decision

What approval means

Recommendation

Approve the local V1 contract and implementation.

The blocking gaps found during this review have been repaired and covered by executable contracts. The central invariant now holds across data, control, Artifact objects, Activity preflight, cold verification, and final receipt recovery.

Boundary to ratify

This is not remote migration support.

Approval accepts local SQLite control and local Artifact authorities only. Remote control/object authorities remain deferred until they have matching typed administration and clean-process evidence.

Reviewer’s one substantive choice:

Ratify local V1 as a complete, honest slice. Do not interpret this change as the Cloudflare/R2 slice described later in the original handoff.

60-second mental model

Migrate each plane. Make Worlds visible last. Prove the result cold.

Planning freezes a typed control snapshot, every current Iceberg table, and every referenced Artifact object. Execution verifies each plane before one last-stage control transaction makes destination Worlds discoverable.

01Gate + freezeLocal endpoints, empty destination, quiescent source, zero Activity history.
02ReserveBind one migration ID to one canonical plan digest.
03Objects + tablesHash objects, migrate all tables, relocate only Artifact object URIs.
04Read back + drift checkSchema, count, digest, source snapshots, control, and inventory must still match.
05 · barrierStage then activateControl rows stage while Worlds remain hidden; directory visibility changes last.
06Cold verifyFresh destination-only process discovers, queries, hashes, resumes, and commits.
07Durable receiptCanonical receipt JSON and digest commit atomically and survive response loss.
plan = await plan_storage_migration(
    source=source_endpoint,
    destination=destination_endpoint,
    migration_id=migration_id,
)
receipt = await migrate_storage(plan)
evidence = await verify_storage_migration(
    receipt,
    destination=destination_endpoint,
)

Contract-first orientation

The four anchors

Behavior

All admitted planes or no success

No partial identity may be reported as successful. Unsupported durable history fails before destination mutation.

Ownership

One orchestration family, two lower participants

archetype.migration owns ordering. Storage owns physical tables/control. Artifacts owns object authority and URI relocation.

Normative source

docs/guide/storage-migration.md

The document defines the local profile, preserved identity, execution barrier, retries, receipt, and trusted cold-verifier obligations.

Executable oracle

Local whole-identity acceptance

Seeds Worlds, lineage, tables, commands, evaluations, outbox, audit, Artifacts, and unknown application state; then proves a fresh destination.

Architecture boundary:

migration → artifacts → storage and migration → storage. Static policy rejects imports into world, commands, activities, runtime, API, CLI, or wiring.

Failure semantics

Retry is evidence-driven, never blind replay

Interruption pointDurable residueExact retry behavior
After object copyVerified content-addressed regular fileRehash and reuse matching bytes; conflict on anything else.
Table commit response unknownTable may or may not contain the planned snapshotRead and digest destination history. Match converges; absence may retry; conflict refuses.
During control stagingOne SQLite transactionAtomic rollback or exact staged digest; Worlds remain undiscoverable.
After activationAll data verified; Worlds visible; reservation ACTIVATEDValidate control extension, recover imported historical snapshots, rerun a retry-safe cold verifier.
After cold tick, before completionLater manifest/fence evidenceVerifier accepts the advanced destination, repeats visible queries, acquires a higher epoch, and commits later.
Completion response lostReservation COMPLETE with canonical receipt JSON + digestReturn the exact stored receipt. Do not rerun cold verification.
Plan binding:

Execution recomputes the canonical plan digest, requires the reservation’s exact plan JSON, rejects extra destination tables, and revalidates status-specific destination control before continuing.

“Nudge nudge” cleanup ledger

Issues found during this review—and fixed before packaging

✓Audit identity omission

An omitted runtime audit config actually means a separate default lakehouse. Endpoints now require explicit co-location and fail closed.

Fixed
✓Lost final receipt

Completion previously stored only a digest. Canonical credential-free receipt JSON now commits atomically and exact retry returns it.

Fixed
✓Late verifier check

A missing cold verifier was discovered after activation. Planning now requires the trusted destination verifier before fencing or mutation.

Fixed
✓Schema and UUID coverage

Logical schema equality now binds order, name, normalized type, and nullability. Native Arrow/Iceberg UUID values are digestible.

Fixed
✓Artifact authority escape

Source URIs bind to the configured root; roots are disjoint; symlinks/directories refuse; destination URIs stay beneath their root.

Fixed
✓Stale or altered plan

Direct execution now verifies canonical plan content, destination inventory, and activated control extension—not only migration ID.

Fixed
✓Acceptance realism

Seeding services are destroyed; migration uses newly composed services; the cold process proves fork-aware queries and repeat verification.

Fixed
✓Dependency security gate

The pre-PR audit found three new aiohttp advisories on the base lock. A surgical quarantine exception upgrades aiohttp to 3.14.3; the vulnerability audit is clean.

Fixed

Evidence nuance: “destination-only” on a local machine
The subprocess receives no source storage path, source Artifact root, source control coordinate, or source capability. The acceptance does not claim an operating-system filesystem sandbox around the temporary parent directory; that stronger isolation belongs with the remote infrastructure slice.
Worktree scope note
The packet reviews the migration implementation against origin/main e08590b2. The workspace branch already contained unrelated Physical AI commits; the migration pull request is cut from a clean branch so those commits are not included.

Approval checklist

Ready when these statements match your intent

V1 means local, offline, whole storage identity.
Destination Iceberg namespace and control identity start empty.
Any Activity history refuses before destination mutation.
Audit and Artifact authorities must be explicit and co-located/disjoint as documented.
Host composition supplies a trusted, retry-safe cold verifier with application code installed.
Remote authorities, source sealing, CLI/REST, and selected-World behavior stay deferred.
Migration administrative reservations are endpoint-local evidence, not recursively moved identity.
The source remains the rollback copy and is never deleted automatically.
Bottom line:

The local slice is now internally consistent, fail-closed at its declared boundaries, crash-recoverable through final acknowledgement, and backed by a destination-only acceptance that queries lineage and advances durable state.
